newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. says Prevlaka on Adriatic stable but tense.
newsitem.headline: U.N. says Prevlaka on Adriatic stable but tense.

text.p: The United Nations said on Friday there was potential for a military clash between Yugoslavia and Croatia in a peninsula south of Dubrovnik and U.N. observers were needed there for another six months.
Most of the Prevlaka peninsula is controlled by Croatia but it borders Yugoslavia's republic of Montenegro and the main deep water port for its navy.
The U.N. mandate expires on Jan. 15 for its 28 military officers.

Despite agreement to demilitarize the peninsula, the report, prepared by Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali before he left office, said violations persisted and warnings by U.N. observers were ignored by both sides.
Croatia has allowed civilians into the area, prompting patrols by Yugoslav naval vessels and accusations that Belgrade's planes had violated Croatian air space.
In addition, Croatia has fortified positions manned by special police and Yugoslavia has a checkpoint. Both sides also have military positions along the international border.
"The continued violations and the lack of real progress on the adoption of the options presented by (the United Nations) are thus cause for concern," the report said.
"Prevlaka remains a stable area. However, as recent events have shown, it is also a tense area and the potential for a military confrontation still exists."
